open_points.subject: ConfirmedOwnerAction correspondence
open_points.text:
`ConfirmedOwnerAction`, the row of the data provider's
`CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS`, is one: its two fields name the confirmed action
(M20, M31) and the owner action (M27), and the rule the table serves — an
action that asks for confirmation is submitted with the confirmation value
the step showed — is fixed by State 2 A13 rule 6 and the `ConfirmedAction`
vocabulary, the closed list of the actions that ask for confirmation
("Identity formats").
open_points.question: For every ConfirmedAction member, which exact OwnerAction member must CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS select? A13 rule 6 governs use of the shown confirmation value, and the vocabulary identifies actions requiring confirmation, but neither stated fact fixes this correspondence.
options: State 2 explicitly lists every ConfirmedAction-to-OwnerAction pair.
The correspondence is derived by an explicit same-name or other deterministic rule.
The contracts choose the pairs when declaring CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS.
open_points.default_guess: List every pair explicitly in State 2 because the correspondence determines which required owner action a confirmed submission performs or refuses.

witness.initial: An owner session holds a pending confirmation for erasing an archived project, bound to the shown confirmation value and erasure inputs.
events: Registry shows the confirmation step to the owner.
The owner submits the shown confirmation value.
The generated owner interface consults CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS to select the owner action.
outcomes: The correspondence selects the project-erasure action and the bound erasure is performed.
A different or absent inferred correspondence selects another owner action or refuses the otherwise valid confirmation.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the confirmed erasure occurs or is refused.

open_points.subject: contract_only row contract representation
open_points.text:
A row of a
constant table may be declared by the contracts alone (`contract_only`), with
no record of its own here, when each of its fields names a fact a model here
already lists and the row itself has no product meaning of its own; its
declaration names where the product rule the table serves is fixed.
open_points.question: What exact contract representation declares a contract_only row, identifies its fields and their existing model facts, and names the design rule that fixes the table's product correspondence?
options: A named contract-only structural type with explicit references to the existing model facts and the fixing rule.
An anonymous tuple or mapping whose key and value types reference the existing model facts, plus structured rule-source metadata.
A dedicated contract declaration kind that emits no model but supplies the row shape and rule-source reference to later generation.
consequences: A named type is easy for notes and checks to identify but may be mistaken for a runtime model unless contract-only status is explicit.
An anonymous shape avoids inventing a model but makes identity, diagnostics and rule-source validation less direct.
A dedicated declaration cleanly preserves the exception but requires State 6 and later generators to understand a new declaration kind.
open_points.requirement:
A row of a
constant table may be declared by the contracts alone (`contract_only`), with
no record of its own here, when each of its fields names a fact a model here
already lists and the row itself has no product meaning of its own; its
declaration names where the product rule the table serves is fixed.
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated contract-only declaration containing the two typed field references and a structured reference to the State 2 rule.
